layer: L1-L6 / Rust mapping of surfaces retired by the D797 kernel set
question: How does graphrefly-rs replace the PULL, PAUSE/RESUME, TEARDOWN, Pausable, kernel-only RESOLVED and Python-only host-boundary surfaces that graphrefly:D798/D799/D800 retire, while the pause, demand, history, checkpoint and restart modules stay root drafts?
decision: Without implementing those modules, in graphrefly-rs:D797-KERNEL-MIGRATION-RS: (1) each pull_id holder (data_structures, messaging, work_queue) exposes a request state node in place of its pull_id and declares it as a dependency; a request is a write to it, with paging or limit params in its value, and the work_queue admission pager writes that state instead of sending PULL up. (2) The pause machinery (LockId, the pause lockset and buffer, Pausable and its source settings) is removed. (3) TEARDOWN and its reactors are removed; SyncValueFromError::Teardown goes, and the sync collector ends on COMPLETE or ERROR. (4) worker.rs sends nothing where it sent [RESOLVED]. (5) HostBoundaryAbort (graphrefly:D431, superseded by graphrefly:D800) is removed with host_boundary.rs and its handlers in the dispatcher, boundary drains, rewire drain, subscribe and batch drains, since only the Python binding armed it. (6) In Rust the retired message types are unrepresentable in process; C-26 and C-42 evidence is that the Message enum has no such variant and Ctx and Node have no upward call, that the crate's canonical wire codec (adapters/bridge_protobuf.rs) carries no Message or Wave, so no retired type can arrive from a peer (its WireEdgeKind DIRTY is renamed PENDING in names only, number 1 unchanged, as spec/protocol.proto does, with the issue codes and status counter named after it; the user chose on 2026-11-10 to do this in phase 1), and that ctx.down, DeferredCtx::down and Node::down reject START, PENDING and RESOLVED at run time (START since graphrefly:D801). (7) The existing checkpoint.rs is changed only where the kernel changes force it and makes no R-checkpoint claim. (8) Host-level Node::replace_deps, subscribe_dep and unsubscribe_dep callers are decided per call site at the start of phase 5. No compatibility path is kept.
rationale: graphrefly:D797 leaves no upward channel and no control message; control is data on a declared edge. A read-only inventory (2026-11-10) found that no production code originates PAUSE, RESUME or TEARDOWN, that the only upward sender is the work_queue admission pager's PULL, that the only non-core RESOLVED sender is worker.rs, and that only crates/graphrefly-bindings-py arms HostBoundaryAbort. The user chose these mappings on 2026-11-10, following graphrefly-ts:D172 where the surfaces match. Corrected the same day before any commit: the first wording said the wire decoder rejects message numbers 8 to 11, but the Rust codec encodes only bridge envelopes and wire-edge frames and has no message decoder.

completion.complete_when: graphrefly-rs:D797-KERNEL-MIGRATION-RS lands these replacements with focused tests and the phase gates pass.
completion.historical_when: A Rust pause, demand, checkpoint or restart module is admitted and replaces the matching mapping.

layer: L1-L6 / Rust host input surface under the D797 kernel set
question: What is the Rust public surface for host input and subscription under graphrefly:D797 (R-wave@2: a wave starts from a host input to a state node), aligned with the TypeScript and Python packages?
decision: (1) Host input exists only on a state handle: Graph::state, Node::state and their empty forms return State<T>, whose set(w), invalidate(), complete() and error(e) are the only host inputs; State<T> gives its Node<T> for subscribing and as a dependency. (2) Node<T> and GraphNode have no public host write: Node::down, GraphNode::down and Node::set are removed; raw arrays leave a node only through ctx.down and DeferredCtx::down. Graph has no host input of its own. (3) A subscriber's sink is Fn(&[Message<AnyValue>]) and is called once per array with the whole array, the START array included. (4) One set writes a value or a function of the value, as R-request-order's set(id, value | fn) does: set(w: impl Into<StateWrite<T>>), where StateWrite<T> is Value(T) or Function(f) with f: FnOnce(Option<&T>) -> Option<T>. A plain value converts by From<T>, so s.set(5) writes 5, always, an equal value included. A function is given as StateWrite::from_fn(f): f receives the state's value when the write runs in request order (None when it has none, as after INVALIDATE), and returning None writes nothing, the Rust form of 'a function that returns the value it was given writes nothing'; Some(v) writes v. Rust has no overloading, and one trait accepting both a value and a closure would overlap for T that is itself a closure, so the function form is a variant of set's argument rather than a second method; a value of a closure type is therefore written as a value, which is the rule's 'a function is written as a value only wrapped in another' turned around: here a function is applied only when wrapped. TypeScript and Python fold the function form into set the same way (the user, 2026-11-10). (5) Timing in graphrefly-rs:D797-KERNEL-MIGRATION-RS: (1) to (3) in phase 2, the function form of set in phase 5. No compatibility path is kept.
rationale: R-wave@2 starts a wave only from a host input to a state node, a batch commit, a function's output or a topology snapshot, so a public down or set on any node is a host input the rules do not have. The user chose, in the cross-runtime alignment session on 2026-11-10, one shared host-input surface for TS, Rust and Python and, for Rust, the Option-returning update recommended by the Rust owner over an Rc identity comparison, since the rule asks only that a function can say 'write nothing' and an explicit None avoids Rc identity in user code. Revised the same day before its commit, after the user folded update into set for every runtime (D797's own wording, missed in the first alignment): the Option-returning function stays, as the function variant of set's argument.

completion.complete_when: graphrefly-rs:D797-KERNEL-MIGRATION-RS phases 2 and 5 land this surface with focused tests.
completion.historical_when: A later Rust decision changes the host input or subscription surface.

layer: L4 / Rust checkpoint stage under graphrefly:D802
question: Does graphrefly-rs:D797-KERNEL-MIGRATION-RS take up the checkpoint module that graphrefly:D802 activated, and what replaces graphrefly-rs:D1 (7)?
decision: Yes. A checkpoint stage follows phase 5 (it builds on setup, replace, ctx.rewire and definition) and brings crates/graphrefly's checkpoint to R-checkpoint@1, as the root handoff's 'Checkpoint after D802' section lists: capture only at a wave boundary (refused inside a wave and inside an open batch body); a restored graph has no subscribers and a restored node receives no waves before its first activation; each node's received inputs per dependency are saved, and at the first activation the function runs once on only the changed dependencies, keeping the saved value otherwise; the setup runs at the restored first activation; recipe and setup belong to the instance, and a replace without a recipe makes the node local-only; each node is built after its declared dependencies and a ctx.rewire's lifetime dependencies are saved; an ended node comes back ended with its dependencies and without private state, with an ERROR payload saved as JSON; the D109 version field and its restore checks leave the checkpoint, and a checkpoint lacking what the rule saves is refused at restore. The layout beyond JSON, its version tag and existing checkpoints are Rust's: the layout changes, its format tag is bumped and older checkpoints are refused. This replaces graphrefly-rs:D1 (7), under which checkpoint.rs changed only where the kernel forced it and made no R-checkpoint claim. C-38 is qualified at the end of the stage; C-45 and C-46 wait for their modules.
rationale: graphrefly:D802 activated R-checkpoint@1 on 2026-11-10 and the user asked earlier that TS and Rust implement checkpoint too; the alignment session relayed the admission, and the user confirmed the continuous plan in this session ('是，按新做法').

completion.complete_when: The checkpoint stage lands with C-38 qualified and the gates pass.
completion.historical_when: A later Rust decision changes the checkpoint layout or scope.

layer: L2 / Rust host reporter under R-failure@3
question: Where does a failure with no caller and no node to end go in the Rust runtime, and what is the host reporter's Rust shape?
decision: A panic from a user sink (Node::subscribe, graph observe) is caught per sink: the fanout goes on to the other sinks and dependents, the node does not end, and the failure goes to the host reporter. The host reporter is one callback per thread, installed with graphrefly::set_host_reporter(Option<HostReporter>) (returns the previous one), where HostReporter = Rc<dyn Fn(&HostFailure)> and HostFailure { source, error }; a sink failure has source "sink". Without a reporter the failure is dropped and nothing is kept; a reporter that panics is ignored. Dependency edges are kernel edges and are not guarded. Cleanup, queued-request and batch failures join the reporter in the phases that own them (phase 4 for cleanup, phase 5 for requests and batch).
rationale: R-failure@3 sends any failure that is not a function's throw or an invalid output to its caller or, with none, to a host reporter callback, and never into an unrelated node; C-34 checks that a sink's throw during a terminal fanout goes to the reporter and is not the node's ERROR. The reference kernel takes the reporter as a graph option; Rust nodes may live outside a Graph (the default arena) and the runtime is single-threaded (each thread owns its waves), so the thread is the host here. The shape is Rust-local: the rule fixes only that the reporter is a callback and that no failure history is kept.

completion.complete_when: Phase 3 lands with C-34's reporter clause qualified.
completion.historical_when: A later Rust decision moves the reporter to the graph or arena.
